canonical_statement: The solvability predicate for finite Post correspondence instances over one fixed binary alphabet is not computable; a solution is one nonempty finite sequence of valid tile indices whose upper and lower word concatenations are equal.
domain_and_universes: PCPInstance = List (List Bool x List Bool); witnesses are List (Fin tiles.length); the target is a Prop in Lean universe 0.
encoding_policy: The input itself is a structured Primcodable finite instance, rather than an external natural-number serialization. Consequently every input is well formed and no malformed-code convention is needed. Bool fixes a nondegenerate two-symbol alphabet independently of the input.

environment_fingerprint.serialization_option: Lean #print default pretty-printer, hashed by check_statement.py

killed: changed the fixed binary alphabet to a unary alphabet
bounded witness length by the number of tiles
allowed different upper and lower index sequences

degenerate_cases: The empty tile list is admitted as a negative instance and checked by emptyInstance_hasNoSolution. Empty words and repeated tiles or indices remain allowed. The empty witness is excluded. Bool prevents unary/empty-alphabet collapse.

alternate_encodings.natural_number_codes: Not selected: a checked encode/decode transport would be required.
alternate_encodings.modified_pcp: Not selected: it requires a checked reduction to ordinary PCP.
alternate_encodings.arbitrary_finite_alphabet: Not selected: the canonical theorem is the standard fixed binary specialization, which expresses uniform PCP undecidability without an alphabet binder.

status_boundary: This freezes and elaborates only the exact binary-PCP undecidability target and its semantic definitions. The checked iff is definitional expansion, not an undecidability proof. Human-source acceptance, anchor audit, proof, validation, release, and master acceptance remain open.
